title: check_revocation and check_revocation_against_anchor largely duplicated
description:
In pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, the CrlChecker's check_revocation (lines 466-690) and check_revocation_against_anchor (lines 718-871) share ~80% identical logic: IDP parsing, indirect-CRL resolution, signer selection, CRL validity check, signature verification, IDP scope check, delta-CRL merge, and revocation-status lookup. The anchor variant differs only in step (2) (anchor identity vs issuer cert) and step (3) (cRLSign check skipped for anchors).

What goes wrong: When a bug is fixed or behavior is changed in one method, the parallel change in the other can be missed. The defense-in-depth comment at line 647 acknowledges some of this duplication. The per-method size (~200 lines each) makes the duplication hard to review.

Similarly in pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs, OcspChecker's check_revocation (lines 142-268) and check_revocation_against_anchor (lines 283-391) have ~70% identical logic.

Locations:
- pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:466-690 and 718-871
- pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:142-268 and 283-391

Recommendation: Extract the shared core into a private helper that takes an 'issuer identity' parameter abstracting over Certificate vs TrustAnchor. The two trait methods become thin adapters that extract the identity and delegate.
